Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Government, viewed as an institution of the state, generally refers to
options: the abstract study of political philosophy alone
the formal machinery, structures, and personnel through which a state exercises its authority and administers its affairs
a purely private organization with no public authority whatsoever
a term applicable exclusively to the judiciary
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: the formal machinery, structures, and personnel through which a state exercises its authority and administers its affairs

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Government, viewed as a process or art of governing, generally refers to
options: a fixed, unchanging institutional structure alone
the ongoing activity of making decisions, formulating policy, and exercising authority to manage the affairs of a state
a term applicable exclusively to elections
a concept with no meaningful practical application
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: the ongoing activity of making decisions, formulating policy, and exercising authority to manage the affairs of a state

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Government, viewed as an academic field of study, generally refers to
options: a purely practical, non- theoretical trade
the systematic scholarly study of political institutions, processes, behaviour, and theory
a field of study limited exclusively to constitutional law
a field that has never actually been recognized as an academic discipline
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: the systematic scholarly study of political institutions, processes, behaviour, and theory

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes government as an institution from government as a process?
options: Government as an institution refers to the formal structures (such as the executive, legislature, and judiciary), while government as a process refers to the ongoing activities and decisions carried out through those structures
The two concepts are entirely identical, with no meaningful distinction
Government as a process refers exclusively to elections, with no broader application
Government as an institution refers exclusively to political parties
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: Government as an institution refers to the formal structures (such as the executive, legislature, and judiciary), while government as a process refers to the ongoing activities and decisions carried out through those structures

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the study of Government as an academic field draws on, and overlaps with, related disciplines such as history, economics, and sociology?
options: Political institutions and processes generally develop and operate in isolation from any other dimension of society
Political phenomena are shaped by, and interact with, historical, economic, and social factors, meaning a full understanding benefits from insights across these related disciplines
Government as an academic field has no meaningful connection to any other discipline
Only historians, rather than political scientists, benefit from studying government
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: Political phenomena are shaped by, and interact with, historical, economic, and social factors, meaning a full understanding benefits from insights across these related disciplines

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding government as an institution alone, without attention to it as a process, would provide an incomplete picture?
options: Formal structures alone do not reveal how decisions are actually made, negotiated, and implemented in practice
The formal structures of government fully and completely explain every aspect of how a state actually operates
Process and institution are, in every respect, entirely unrelated concepts
Understanding government as a process provides no additional insight beyond studying its institutions
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: Formal structures alone do not reveal how decisions are actually made, negotiated, and implemented in practice

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: The scope of the study of Government generally includes
options: exclusively the study of foreign policy, with no attention to domestic institutions
the study of the state, its institutions, political processes, citizenship, political behaviour, and relations among states
exclusively economic policy, with no attention to political institutions
a scope limited exclusively to the study of elections
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: the study of the state, its institutions, political processes, citizenship, political behaviour, and relations among states

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the study of Government is considered relevant to producing informed, participatory citizens, one of the aims articulated within the WAEC syllabus?
options: Understanding how government works, and citizens’ rights and duties within it, equips individuals to participate meaningfully in civic and political life
Studying government has no meaningful connection to how citizens actually participate in civic life
Only elected officials, rather than ordinary citizens, benefit from studying government
Civic participation is entirely unrelated to any understanding of political institutions or processes
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: Understanding how government works, and citizens’ rights and duties within it, equips individuals to participate meaningfully in civic and political life

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why evaluating the successes, failures, and problems of governments in West Africa, another aim articulated within the WAEC syllabus, requires more than simply memorizing institutional structures?
options: A meaningful evaluation requires examining how institutions have actually performed in practice, including their historical achievements and shortcomings, not merely their formal design
Institutional structures alone, considered in isolation from practical performance, fully determine whether a government should be judged a success or failure
Evaluating government performance has no meaningful connection to historical practice
Formal design and practical performance are, in every respect, identical considerations
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: A meaningful evaluation requires examining how institutions have actually performed in practice, including their historical achievements and shortcomings, not merely their formal design

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the study of Government, as an academic field, generally distinguishes between descriptive analysis (how government actually functions) and normative evaluation (how government ought to function)?
options: Descriptive and normative approaches serve differing purposes: description explains actual institutional practice, while normative evaluation assesses that practice against ideals such as justice or effectiveness, and a well-rounded study benefits from both
Description and evaluation are, in every respect, identical approaches with no useful distinction
Normative evaluation has no legitimate place within the academic study of government
Descriptive analysis alone, without any normative dimension, fully captures everything of value within the study of government
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: Descriptive and normative approaches serve differing purposes: description explains actual institutional practice, while normative evaluation assesses that practice against ideals such as justice or effectiveness, and a well-rounded study benefits from both

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding government as an academic field of study is considered a useful foundation before proceeding to study more specific concepts and principles of government, examined in the following topic?
options: The broader conceptual and disciplinary framework provided by this foundational topic provides context for meaningfully approaching the more specific concepts, principles, and institutions examined subsequently
This foundational topic has no meaningful connection to any subsequent topic within the broader study of government
Specific concepts and principles of government can be fully understood without any foundational understanding of government as a broader field
Foundational and specific topics within the study of government are entirely unrelated
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: The broader conceptual and disciplinary framework provided by this foundational topic provides context for meaningfully approaching the more specific concepts, principles, and institutions examined subsequently

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why government, considered as an institution, is generally regarded as encompassing more than simply the executive branch alone?
options: The term generally refers to the complete set of formal structures through which state authority is exercised, encompassing the legislature and judiciary alongside the executive, rather than the executive alone
The term “government,” properly understood, refers exclusively and only to the executive branch, with no meaningful reference to the legislature or judiciary
The legislature and judiciary generally fall outside the scope of what is properly considered “government”
There is, in practice, no meaningful institutional distinction between the executive, legislature, and judiciary
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: The term generally refers to the complete set of formal structures through which state authority is exercised, encompassing the legislature and judiciary alongside the executive, rather than the executive alone

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why some scholars argue that studying government as a “process” is particularly important for understanding how policy actually emerges, beyond simply knowing which institution is formally responsible for a given decision?
options: Formal institutional responsibility does not fully capture the negotiation, compromise, and practical dynamics through which policy is actually shaped and implemented
The process through which policy emerges is, in every respect, entirely determined by formal institutional responsibility alone
Studying government as a process provides no meaningful additional insight beyond simply identifying the formally responsible institution
Policy emergence has no meaningful connection to any process-oriented analysis
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: Formal institutional responsibility does not fully capture the negotiation, compromise, and practical dynamics through which policy is actually shaped and implemented

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the WAEC syllabus’s stated aim of helping candidates “appreciate the role of his country as a member of the international community” connects the study of domestic government to the study of international relations, examined later in Section B?
options: A country’s domestic governmental structure and its participation in international affairs are generally interconnected, meaning a complete understanding of government benefits from studying both dimensions together
Domestic government and international relations are, in every respect, entirely separate and unrelated subjects
International relations has no meaningful connection to the broader study of Government as an academic subject
Only domestic institutions, to the exclusion of any international dimension, are properly within the scope of the study of Government
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: A country’s domestic governmental structure and its participation in international affairs are generally interconnected, meaning a complete understanding of government benefits from studying both dimensions together

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding government as encompassing both institutions and processes is considered particularly important for critically evaluating whether a given country’s government is functioning effectively?
options: An effective evaluation requires examining both the formal design of institutions and how decisions are actually made and implemented in practice, since either dimension alone would provide an incomplete assessment
Effective evaluation of a government’s functioning requires attention exclusively to its formal institutional design, with no meaningful reference to how decisions are actually made in practice
The formal design of institutions and the practical process of decision-making are, in every respect, identical considerations requiring no separate attention
Evaluating a government’s effectiveness has no meaningful connection to either its institutional design or its decision- making processes
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: An effective evaluation requires examining both the formal design of institutions and how decisions are actually made and implemented in practice, since either dimension alone would provide an incomplete assessment

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the WAEC syllabus places the “meaning and scope” of Government as its opening topic, before proceeding to specific concepts, principles, and institutions?
options: Establishing a clear shared understanding of what the subject actually encompasses provides an appropriate conceptual starting point before students proceed to more specific, detailed content
The ordering of syllabus topics has no meaningful pedagogical rationale whatsoever
Specific concepts and institutions are, in every respect, more foundational than a general understanding of the subject’s meaning and scope
There is no meaningful reason to establish a shared understanding of a subject’s scope before studying its specific content
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: Establishing a clear shared understanding of what the subject actually encompasses provides an appropriate conceptual starting point before students proceed to more specific, detailed content

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why government as an academic field is generally considered an empirical as well as a theoretical discipline?
options: The field draws on real-world observation and evidence about how political institutions and processes actually function, in addition to engaging with abstract theoretical frameworks
Government as an academic field is purely theoretical, with no meaningful empirical or evidence-based dimension whatsoever
Empirical observation has no legitimate place within the academic study of government
Theoretical frameworks and empirical observation are, in every respect, entirely unrelated to one another within the discipline
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: The field draws on real-world observation and evidence about how political institutions and processes actually function, in addition to engaging with abstract theoretical frameworks

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding government as a “process” is considered especially relevant for comprehending how a bill becomes law, a specific topic examined later under Organs of Government?
options: The process of law-making involves a sequence of institutional actions and decisions, meaning understanding government as an ongoing process helps illuminate how this specific sequence actually unfolds
The process of a bill becoming law has no meaningful connection to the broader concept of government as a process
Understanding government purely as a fixed institution, with no attention to process, fully explains how a bill becomes law
Law-making is, in every respect, an entirely static, rather than a dynamic or process-oriented, phenomenon
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: The process of law-making involves a sequence of institutional actions and decisions, meaning understanding government as an ongoing process helps illuminate how this specific sequence actually unfolds

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a well-rounded understanding of the meaning and scope of Government is considered valuable preparation for the WASSCE Government examination as a whole, given the exam’s coverage of both Section A and Section B topics?
options: A clear grasp of the subject’s overall meaning and scope helps students situate the more specific Section A and Section B topics within a coherent overall framework, rather than approaching each topic as an isolated, disconnected fact
The meaning and scope of Government has no meaningful bearing on how well students perform on the specific Section A and Section B content examined within the WASSCE Government paper
Section A and Section B topics are, in every respect, entirely unrelated to the broader question of what Government, as a subject, actually encompasses
Students can achieve an equally strong understanding of Section A and Section B content without any prior grounding in the subject’s overall meaning and scope
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: A clear grasp of the subject’s overall meaning and scope helps students situate the more specific Section A and Section B topics within a coherent overall framework, rather than approaching each topic as an isolated, disconnected fact

Meaning and Scope of Government.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the overall importance of understanding the meaning and scope of Government as an institution, a process, and an academic field of study?
options: A clear understanding of these three dimensions provides the essential conceptual foundation for the more specific concepts, principles, institutions, and comparative West African political developments examined throughout the remainder of this syllabus
Understanding the meaning and scope of Government has no meaningful practical or academic value within the broader study of the subject
Only one of these three dimensions (institution, process, or academic field) is genuinely worthy of serious study, to the exclusion of the other two
The meaning and scope of Government bears no meaningful relationship to the subject’s more specific subsequent content
Meaning and Scope of Government.correct_answer: A clear understanding of these three dimensions provides the essential conceptual foundation for the more specific concepts, principles, institutions, and comparative West African political developments examined throughout the remainder of this syllabus

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Power, in political science, is generally defined as
options: the legal right to rule granted by a constitution alone
the ability to influence or control the behaviour of others, with or without their consent
the moral acceptance of a ruler by the governed
a concept applicable exclusively to military institutions
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: the ability to influence or control the behaviour of others, with or without their consent

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Authority differs from power mainly in that authority is
options: power exercised without any legal or moral backing whatsoever
power that is recognized as legitimate and rightfully exercised
identical to power in every meaningful respect
a concept exercised exclusively by military rulers
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: power that is recognized as legitimate and rightfully exercised

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Legitimacy generally refers to
options: the physical capacity of a government to enforce its will through coercion alone
the general acceptance of a government’s right to rule by the people it governs
a quality possessed only by governments recognized internationally
a quality found exclusively in democratic systems
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: the general acceptance of a government’s right to rule by the people it governs

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Sovereignty is generally defined as
options: the supreme and final authority of a state over its territory and people, both internally and externally
a state’s ability to trade freely with other nations
a quality applicable exclusively to the executive branch
a term identical in every respect to legitimacy
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: the supreme and final authority of a state over its territory and people, both internally and externally

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Democracy, in its broadest sense, refers to a system of government in which
options: power is held by a single unelected ruler
political power ultimately derives from the people, typically exercised through free elections and protection of civil liberties
power is inherited exclusively through bloodline
only the wealthy are permitted to participate in governance
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: political power ultimately derives from the people, typically exercised through free elections and protection of civil liberties

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Political culture generally refers to
options: the artistic traditions of a given community
the shared pattern of political attitudes, values, beliefs, and orientations held by members of a political community
the formal legal structure of a country’s government
a term synonymous with political party membership
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: the shared pattern of political attitudes, values, beliefs, and orientations held by members of a political community

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Political socialization refers to the process by which
options: individuals acquire their political values, beliefs, and attitudes, typically through family, school, media, and other social institutions
political parties are formally registered
a government transitions from one regime to another
citizens are formally stripped of voting rights
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: individuals acquire their political values, beliefs, and attitudes, typically through family, school, media, and other social institutions

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Communalism, as a mode of social and economic organization, is generally characterized by
options: private individual ownership of all land and resources
collective ownership and communal use of land and resources by the wider community, typical of many pre-industrial West African societies
rule by a single hereditary monarch over all economic activity
a system based entirely on factory-based wage labour
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: collective ownership and communal use of land and resources by the wider community, typical of many pre-industrial West African societies

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Socialism is an ideology generally characterized by
options: exclusively private ownership of the means of production
significant collective or state ownership and control of the means of production, with an emphasis on reducing economic inequality
a complete absence of any government whatsoever
rule by a hereditary aristocracy
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: significant collective or state ownership and control of the means of production, with an emphasis on reducing economic inequality

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Communism, as envisioned in Marxist theory, is generally characterized by
options: the establishment of a classless, stateless society in which the means of production are held in common
the strict, permanent preservation of private capitalist ownership of industry
rule by a hereditary aristocracy over economic decisions
the complete absence of any economic organization whatsoever
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: the establishment of a classless, stateless society in which the means of production are held in common

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Capitalism is an ideology generally characterized by
options: state ownership of all means of production
private ownership of the means of production, with economic activity primarily driven by market forces and profit
communal ownership of land, with no private property
rule by a hereditary monarch over all economic decisions
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: private ownership of the means of production, with economic activity primarily driven by market forces and profit

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Feudalism was a socio-economic and political system generally characterized by
options: a classless society with no hierarchy of any kind
a hierarchical system in which land was held by lords in exchange for service, with peasants (serfs) working the land under obligation to a lord
collective ownership of all property by the entire community
rule by an elected parliament with no monarch or nobility whatsoever
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: a hierarchical system in which land was held by lords in exchange for service, with peasants (serfs) working the land under obligation to a lord

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Fascism is a political ideology generally characterized by
options: extreme individualism and minimal government authority
authoritarian ultranationalism, typically combined with dictatorial government and suppression of political opposition
collective, classless ownership of property with no state authority
a strictly limited government focused solely on protecting civil liberties
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: authoritarian ultranationalism, typically combined with dictatorial government and suppression of political opposition

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Nazism refers specifically to the ideology of the National Socialist German Workers’ Party, generally characterized by
options: a commitment to individual liberty and multi-party democracy
an extreme, racially based form of fascism, combining totalitarian control and a genocidal racial ideology
a purely economic ideology with no political dimension whatsoever
a system based on communal, classless ownership of all property
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: an extreme, racially based form of fascism, combining totalitarian control and a genocidal racial ideology

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Totalitarianism is generally characterized by
options: extensive individual liberty with minimal state interference in private life
an all-encompassing state control over virtually all aspects of public and private life, typically enforced through a single ruling party
a strictly limited government with power widely distributed among competing institutions
rule exclusively by an elected, multi-party parliament with strong civil liberty protections
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: an all-encompassing state control over virtually all aspects of public and private life, typically enforced through a single ruling party

Basic Concepts of Government.text: A society, in political terms, generally refers to
options: a group of people who share a common government and defined territory
a group of people living together, sharing common customs, traditions, and social relationships, not necessarily under a single government
a term identical in every respect to “state”
a purely economic unit with no cultural dimension
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: a group of people living together, sharing common customs, traditions, and social relationships, not necessarily under a single government

Basic Concepts of Government.text: A state is generally defined as
options: a group sharing common customs but with no defined territory
a political and legal entity possessing a defined territory, population, government, and sovereignty
a term identical in every respect to “nation”
any organization that collects taxes
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: a political and legal entity possessing a defined territory, population, government, and sovereignty

Basic Concepts of Government.text: A nation refers to
options: a group of people bound together by a defined territory and government alone
a group of people who share a common identity, often based on shared language, culture, history, or ethnicity, regardless of political boundaries
a term identical in every respect to “state”
only a group recognized by the United Nations
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: a group of people who share a common identity, often based on shared language, culture, history, or ethnicity, regardless of political boundaries

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Colonialism generally refers to
options: a system in which one state or people establish and maintain political and economic control over another territory and its people
a purely voluntary trade partnership between two equal states
a form of government exercised exclusively by an indigenous ruling class
a term with no meaningful application to West African history
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: a system in which one state or people establish and maintain political and economic control over another territory and its people

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Nationalism, in the context of the WAEC syllabus’s treatment of West African political development, generally refers to
options: an entirely apolitical cultural movement with no connection to political independence
a political movement or sentiment aimed at achieving self-determination and independence for a particular people or territory, often in opposition to colonial rule
a movement aimed exclusively at strengthening colonial administrative control
a term applicable exclusively to European political movements
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: a political movement or sentiment aimed at achieving self-determination and independence for a particular people or territory, often in opposition to colonial rule

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes power from authority?
options: Power always requires legitimacy, while authority does not
Power is the raw capacity to compel behaviour, whereas authority is power exercised with a recognized right to do so
They are identical concepts, used interchangeably in political science
Authority can never be backed by power
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Power is the raw capacity to compel behaviour, whereas authority is power exercised with a recognized right to do so

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a nation from a state?
options: A nation is defined strictly by legal and territorial boundaries, while a state is defined by shared culture
A nation is based primarily on shared identity, while a state is a political and legal entity with defined territory and government
The two terms are entirely interchangeable, with no meaningful distinction
A nation must always possess its own government, while a state need not
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: A nation is based primarily on shared identity, while a state is a political and legal entity with defined territory and government

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why sovereignty is generally considered a defining characteristic distinguishing a fully independent state from a colonial territory?
options: Sovereignty, both internal and external, indicates supreme authority over a territory’s own affairs and independence from external control, qualities generally absent under colonial administration
Sovereignty is irrelevant to whether a territory qualifies as a fully independent state
A colonial territory automatically possesses full sovereignty
Only states recognized by every other state in the world can be considered sovereign
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Sovereignty, both internal and external, indicates supreme authority over a territory’s own affairs and independence from external control, qualities generally absent under colonial administration

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains the general Marxist critique of capitalism that underpins socialist and communist ideology?
options: Marxist theory generally argues that capitalism inherently produces exploitation of the working class and significant economic inequality, which socialism and communism seek to address through collective or state ownership
Marxist theory generally argues that capitalism produces perfectly equal outcomes for all members of society
Marxist critique of capitalism has no meaningful connection to the origins of socialist or communist ideology
Capitalism, according to Marxist theory, eliminates the concept of social class entirely
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Marxist theory generally argues that capitalism inherently produces exploitation of the working class and significant economic inequality, which socialism and communism seek to address through collective or state ownership

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why totalitarianism is generally distinguished from a more limited form of authoritarianism?
options: Totalitarianism generally seeks to control virtually all aspects of public and private life in service of a particular ideology, whereas a more limited authoritarian regime may restrict political freedoms while leaving greater areas of private life comparatively less regulated
Totalitarianism and authoritarianism are entirely identical concepts, with no meaningful distinction
Totalitarian regimes generally impose fewer restrictions on private life than authoritarian regimes
Authoritarian regimes always permit full multi-party democratic competition, unlike totalitarian regimes
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Totalitarianism generally seeks to control virtually all aspects of public and private life in service of a particular ideology, whereas a more limited authoritarian regime may restrict political freedoms while leaving greater areas of private life comparatively less regulated

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why communalism, as traditionally practised in many pre- colonial West African societies, is sometimes cited in discussions of alternative economic organization to Western capitalism?
options: Communalism’s emphasis on collective land ownership and communal social obligation is sometimes contrasted with capitalism’s emphasis on private property and individual economic competition
Communalism, as traditionally practised, shares an identical economic structure with modern Western capitalism
Communalism has no meaningful historical or theoretical relevance to discussions of alternative economic organization
Pre-colonial West African societies never practised any form of communal land ownership
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Communalism’s emphasis on collective land ownership and communal social obligation is sometimes contrasted with capitalism’s emphasis on private property and individual economic competition

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why colonialism is generally considered closely connected to the subsequent emergence of nationalism in West Africa?
options: Colonial political and economic domination generated grievances and aspirations for self-rule among colonized peoples, which directly fuelled the growth of nationalist movements seeking independence
Colonialism generally had no meaningful connection whatsoever to the subsequent emergence of nationalist movements in West Africa
Nationalism in West Africa emerged entirely independently of, and prior to, any experience of colonial rule
Colonial administration and nationalist sentiment are, in every respect, entirely unrelated historical phenomena
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Colonial political and economic domination generated grievances and aspirations for self-rule among colonized peoples, which directly fuelled the growth of nationalist movements seeking independence

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding political socialization is important for understanding a society’s broader political culture?
options: Through political socialization, individuals absorb the shared values, beliefs, and attitudes that collectively constitute a society’s political culture
Political socialization has no meaningful bearing on a society’s political culture
Political culture is fixed at a nation’s founding and cannot be influenced by socialization
Political socialization occurs only among elected officials
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Through political socialization, individuals absorb the shared values, beliefs, and attitudes that collectively constitute a society’s political culture

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why fascism and communism, despite both being associated historically with totalitarian control, are generally considered ideologically opposed to one another?
options: Fascism generally emphasizes nationalist unity and, often, private property under strong state direction, while communism generally emphasizes international class solidarity and the abolition of private ownership of the means of production
Fascism and communism are, in every meaningful respect, identical ideologies with no useful distinction between them
Fascism generally advocates for the same internationalist, classless goals as communism
Communism generally advocates for private property and nationalist unity, in the same manner as fascism
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Fascism generally emphasizes nationalist unity and, often, private property under strong state direction, while communism generally emphasizes international class solidarity and the abolition of private ownership of the means of production

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the concept of sovereignty is particularly significant within the study of West African political development, given the region’s colonial history?
options: The transition from colonial rule (in which sovereignty rested with the colonial power) to independence (in which sovereignty was transferred to the new state) represents a defining feature of the region’s twentieth-century political history
Sovereignty is a concept with no particular relevance to West African political history
West African states never actually acquired sovereignty at any point in their history
Colonial powers generally retained sovereignty over West African territories even after formal independence was granted
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: The transition from colonial rule (in which sovereignty rested with the colonial power) to independence (in which sovereignty was transferred to the new state) represents a defining feature of the region’s twentieth-century political history

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a multi-ethnic West African state may face particular challenges in developing a strong overarching sense of nationhood, distinct from more localized ethnic identity?
options: Where multiple distinct ethnic or cultural groups exist within a single state’s borders, a shared overarching national identity may take considerable time and deliberate effort to develop, compared to a more culturally homogeneous state
Multi-ethnic composition automatically guarantees strong national unity
Ethnic diversity has no bearing whatsoever on nation-building
A state can never achieve nationhood if it contains more than one ethnic group
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Where multiple distinct ethnic or cultural groups exist within a single state’s borders, a shared overarching national identity may take considerable time and deliberate effort to develop, compared to a more culturally homogeneous state

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why democracy is generally regarded as more accountable than totalitarianism?
options: Regular elections and independent institutions in a democracy allow citizens to remove leaders who perform poorly or abuse power, a mechanism generally absent under totalitarian rule
Totalitarian regimes generally provide more effective accountability mechanisms than democracies
Accountability is irrelevant to the classification of political systems
Democracies never hold their leaders accountable in any meaningful way
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Regular elections and independent institutions in a democracy allow citizens to remove leaders who perform poorly or abuse power, a mechanism generally absent under totalitarian rule

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why legitimacy is generally considered distinct from mere power, even though a legitimate government typically also possesses power?
options: A government can possess power (the capacity to compel behaviour through force) without necessarily being regarded by its people as having a rightful claim to rule, which is the essence of legitimacy
Power and legitimacy are always identical, so this distinction could never meaningfully arise
A government automatically loses all power the moment it loses legitimacy
Legitimacy is granted only by international bodies, never by a state’s own citizens
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: A government can possess power (the capacity to compel behaviour through force) without necessarily being regarded by its people as having a rightful claim to rule, which is the essence of legitimacy

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the historical evolution of many West African societies from communalism, through colonial-era capitalist penetration, to varying post-independence experiments with socialism and market economics, illustrates a broader pattern in the region’s economic and political history?
options: This historical trajectory illustrates how differing economic ideologies have been successively adopted, adapted, or contested at different points in the region’s political and economic development, reflecting changing historical circumstances and policy priorities
West African economic systems have, in fact, remained entirely fixed and unchanging throughout the region’s entire history, with no meaningful ideological variation whatsoever
Communalism, capitalism, and socialism are, in every respect, identical economic systems with no useful distinction between them
Colonial-era economic policy generally had no meaningful connection whatsoever to subsequent post-independence economic policy choices in West Africa
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: This historical trajectory illustrates how differing economic ideologies have been successively adopted, adapted, or contested at different points in the region’s political and economic development, reflecting changing historical circumstances and policy priorities

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the term “nationalism” can carry a somewhat differing specific connotation when applied to anti-colonial movements in West Africa, compared to its application in, for example, interwar European contexts?
options: In the West African anti-colonial context, nationalism generally centred on the goal of self-determination and independence from foreign colonial rule, whereas in other historical contexts nationalism has sometimes been associated with more exclusionary or expansionist aims, meaning the term’s specific connotation can vary somewhat by historical context
Nationalism carries an entirely identical specific connotation in every possible historical context, with no meaningful variation whatsoever
West African anti-colonial nationalism generally had no meaningful connection whatsoever to the broader general concept of nationalism
The specific historical context in which nationalism arises generally has no bearing on how that particular nationalist movement’s specific aims are properly understood
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: In the West African anti-colonial context, nationalism generally centred on the goal of self-determination and independence from foreign colonial rule, whereas in other historical contexts nationalism has sometimes been associated with more exclusionary or expansionist aims, meaning the term’s specific connotation can vary somewhat by historical context

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why political culture can differ meaningfully between countries even where those countries share broadly similar formal governmental institutions?
options: Political culture reflects a society’s underlying attitudes, values, and historical experience, which can differ significantly even where the formal institutional structure (such as a presidential system) is broadly similar across countries
Political culture is, in every respect, entirely determined by formal institutional structure alone, with no independent variation possible
Countries sharing broadly similar formal institutions always share an entirely identical political culture
Political culture has no meaningful connection whatsoever to a society’s underlying attitudes or historical experience
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Political culture reflects a society’s underlying attitudes, values, and historical experience, which can differ significantly even where the formal institutional structure (such as a presidential system) is broadly similar across countries

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why some newly independent West African states, in the years following independence, experimented with socialist-inspired economic policies?
options: Socialist-inspired policies were sometimes seen as a means of pursuing rapid national economic development and reducing perceived inequalities inherited from the colonial economic structure
Socialist-inspired economic policies have, in fact, never been adopted or experimented with by any newly independent West African state
State ownership of key industries has no meaningful connection to broader socialist ideological principles
Post-colonial economic policy choices generally have no meaningful connection to a state’s particular ideological orientation
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Socialist-inspired policies were sometimes seen as a means of pursuing rapid national economic development and reducing perceived inequalities inherited from the colonial economic structure

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding the concept of “state,” as distinct from “nation” and “society,” is particularly important when analysing West African countries whose current borders were substantially shaped by colonial-era boundary decisions, rather than by pre-existing ethnic or national divisions?
options: Many West African states’ formal territorial boundaries were drawn during the colonial period without close regard to pre-existing ethnic or national groupings, meaning the formal “state” and the underlying “nation(s)” or “society/societies” within it may not neatly coincide
Every West African state’s formal boundaries, in fact, precisely and exactly coincide with a single, pre-existing, unified nation
The distinction between state, nation, and society has no meaningful relevance to understanding West African political geography
Colonial-era boundary decisions generally had no meaningful connection whatsoever to the later territorial structure of independent West African states
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Many West African states’ formal territorial boundaries were drawn during the colonial period without close regard to pre-existing ethnic or national groupings, meaning the formal “state” and the underlying “nation(s)” or “society/societies” within it may not neatly coincide

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why totalitarian and fascist ideologies are generally considered incompatible with the broader principle of representative government, examined later within this syllabus’s treatment of basic principles?
options: Totalitarian and fascist systems generally concentrate power in a single ruling party or leader and suppress political competition, directly contradicting representative government’s core requirement that citizens elect accountable representatives through competitive elections
Totalitarian and fascist ideologies are, in fact, fully compatible with, and indistinguishable from, representative government
Representative government has no meaningful connection whatsoever to the broader classification of political ideologies
Political competition and citizen accountability are irrelevant considerations when evaluating whether a system qualifies as totalitarian or fascist
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Totalitarian and fascist systems generally concentrate power in a single ruling party or leader and suppress political competition, directly contradicting representative government’s core requirement that citizens elect accountable representatives through competitive elections

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding basic concepts such as power, authority, legitimacy, and sovereignty provides essential groundwork for the subsequent study of constitutions, examined in the following topic?
options: Constitutions are fundamentally concerned with allocating and constraining power and authority and defining a state’s sovereign structure, meaning a prior grasp of these basic concepts is genuinely useful preparation for meaningfully studying constitutions
Constitutions have no meaningful connection whatsoever to the basic concepts of power, authority, legitimacy, or sovereignty
A prior understanding of these basic concepts provides no useful preparatory value whatsoever for subsequently studying constitutions
Power, authority, legitimacy, and sovereignty are, in every respect, entirely unrelated to how constitutions are actually structured or understood
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Constitutions are fundamentally concerned with allocating and constraining power and authority and defining a state’s sovereign structure, meaning a prior grasp of these basic concepts is genuinely useful preparation for meaningfully studying constitutions

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a government reliant primarily on coercion, rather than legitimacy, is often considered less stable over the long term?
options: Reliance on force alone, without broader acceptance of the government’s right to rule, tends to generate resentment and resistance, making such regimes more vulnerable to instability
Coercive rule generally provokes no resistance whatsoever from the governed population
Coercion always guarantees indefinite political stability
Legitimacy has no bearing on a government’s long-term survival
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Reliance on force alone, without broader acceptance of the government’s right to rule, tends to generate resentment and resistance, making such regimes more vulnerable to instability

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why capitalism and socialism are often understood as existing along a spectrum, rather than as a rigid binary choice?
options: In practice, many real-world economic systems incorporate varying degrees of private market activity and state intervention, meaning most actual economies fall somewhere along a continuum, rather than fitting neatly into one pure category
Every real- world economic system fits perfectly and exclusively into either a purely capitalist or a purely socialist category
The concept of a spectrum has no meaningful analytical relevance to comparing differing economic ideologies
Capitalism and socialism, as ideological categories, admit no meaningful variation whatsoever
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: In practice, many real-world economic systems incorporate varying degrees of private market activity and state intervention, meaning most actual economies fall somewhere along a continuum, rather than fitting neatly into one pure category

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why Nazism is generally distinguished from other, more general forms of fascism by its particularly extreme emphasis on racial ideology?
options: While sharing certain broader fascist characteristics such as ultranationalism and authoritarian control, Nazism specifically incorporated a distinctive and extreme racial ideology culminating in genocide, a feature not equally present within every general form of fascism
Nazism and other forms of fascism are, in every ideological respect, entirely identical, with no meaningful distinguishing features
Racial ideology played no meaningful role whatsoever in distinguishing Nazism from other forms of fascism
The Holocaust had no meaningful historical connection to the specific ideological content of Nazism
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: While sharing certain broader fascist characteristics such as ultranationalism and authoritarian control, Nazism specifically incorporated a distinctive and extreme racial ideology culminating in genocide, a feature not equally present within every general form of fascism

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding the concept of “colonialism” is essential preparatory background for the WAEC syllabus’s later, more detailed treatment of colonial administration in West Africa?
options: A clear grasp of colonialism’s general meaning provides the necessary conceptual foundation for understanding the specific colonial administrative policies (such as indirect rule or assimilation) examined in more detail later within this syllabus
Colonialism, as a general concept, has no meaningful connection whatsoever to the specific colonial administrative policies examined later within this syllabus
The specific colonial administrative policies examined later within this syllabus can be fully understood without any prior general understanding of colonialism
General concepts and their more specific subsequent applications are, in every respect, entirely unrelated within the study of Government
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: A clear grasp of colonialism’s general meaning provides the necessary conceptual foundation for understanding the specific colonial administrative policies (such as indirect rule or assimilation) examined in more detail later within this syllabus

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why “society,” as a broader sociological concept, is generally considered distinguishable from “state,” even though the two terms are sometimes used loosely and interchangeably in everyday speech?
options: A society can exist without a formal government or defined political boundaries, whereas a state specifically requires a government, defined territory, and sovereignty
A society and a state are always identical, with no meaningful distinction
A state can exist without any population whatsoever
Society refers exclusively to economic relationships, with no cultural dimension
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: A society can exist without a formal government or defined political boundaries, whereas a state specifically requires a government, defined territory, and sovereignty

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why power is generally considered a more fundamental, broader concept than legitimacy within political analysis, even though legitimacy is often considered a more desirable quality for a government to possess?
options: Power can exist and be exercised, whether legitimately or illegitimately, whereas legitimacy specifically refers to a normatively significant subset of power exercised with a recognized rightful claim, meaning power is the broader underlying category
Legitimacy is a broader concept than power, encompassing every possible exercise of power within its scope
Power and legitimacy are, in every respect, identical concepts with no meaningful hierarchy or relationship between them
A government must always possess legitimacy before it can be said to possess any power whatsoever
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Power can exist and be exercised, whether legitimately or illegitimately, whereas legitimacy specifically refers to a normatively significant subset of power exercised with a recognized rightful claim, meaning power is the broader underlying category

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the concept of the “nation-state” is sometimes considered an aspiration rather than a fully achieved reality for many West African countries?
options: A nation- state ideally involves a state whose population largely shares a single common national identity coinciding with its borders, a condition not fully met by many West African states given their considerable internal ethnic diversity inherited from colonial-era boundary drawing
Every West African state, without exception, already fully and completely qualifies as a nation-state in the strictest sense
The concept of a nation-state has no meaningful relevance whatsoever to West African political geography
Ethnic diversity within a state’s borders has no bearing whatsoever on whether that state qualifies as a nation-state
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: A nation- state ideally involves a state whose population largely shares a single common national identity coinciding with its borders, a condition not fully met by many West African states given their considerable internal ethnic diversity inherited from colonial-era boundary drawing

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding differing economic and political ideologies (capitalism, socialism, communism, fascism, totalitarianism) is considered valuable background for analysing the policy choices of specific West African governments examined later within this syllabus?
options: A government’s underlying ideological orientation often significantly shapes its specific policy choices, such as its approach to economic management or political competition, making ideological analysis a genuinely useful tool for understanding specific historical governments
A government’s underlying ideological orientation has no meaningful bearing whatsoever on its specific policy choices
Every West African government, regardless of ideological orientation, pursues an entirely identical set of policy choices
Ideological analysis is relevant only to European political history, with no bearing on West African political analysis
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: A government’s underlying ideological orientation often significantly shapes its specific policy choices, such as its approach to economic management or political competition, making ideological analysis a genuinely useful tool for understanding specific historical governments

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why colonialism is generally distinguished from more general forms of international economic or political influence, such as ordinary trade relations between two sovereign states?
options: Colonialism specifically involves the establishment of direct political and administrative control by one state over another territory and its people, going beyond the more limited economic influence typically involved in ordinary trade relations between sovereign equals
Colonialism and ordinary trade relations between sovereign states are, in every respect, identical phenomena with no useful distinction
Political and administrative control has no meaningful bearing on whether a particular relationship is properly classified as colonial
Colonialism, properly understood, never involves any meaningful economic dimension whatsoever
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Colonialism specifically involves the establishment of direct political and administrative control by one state over another territory and its people, going beyond the more limited economic influence typically involved in ordinary trade relations between sovereign equals

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why some scholars argue that certain values evident within traditional West African communalism, such as an emphasis on collective welfare, continued to influence political and social thought in the region even after significant colonial-era and post-independence economic transformation?
options: Deeply rooted traditional values and social patterns often persist and continue to shape a society’s political and social thought even amid significant subsequent economic or institutional change, rather than being entirely displaced by that change
Traditional communalist values were, in fact, entirely and immediately eliminated the moment colonial-era economic transformation began, leaving no meaningful lasting influence whatsoever
Political and social thought in West Africa developed entirely independently of, and with no meaningful connection whatsoever to, any traditional communalist values
Deeply rooted traditional values generally have no meaningful capacity whatsoever to persist or influence subsequent political or social thought
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Deeply rooted traditional values and social patterns often persist and continue to shape a society’s political and social thought even amid significant subsequent economic or institutional change, rather than being entirely displaced by that change

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why “political socialization” and “political culture” are closely related but analytically distinct concepts?
options: Political socialization refers to the process through which individuals acquire political values and attitudes, while political culture refers to the resulting broader shared pattern of such values and attitudes across a given society, meaning the two concepts describe a process and its resulting outcome respectively
Political socialization and political culture are, in every respect, entirely identical concepts, with no meaningful distinction whatsoever
Political culture refers exclusively to an individual’s own personal political values, with no broader societal dimension whatsoever
Political socialization has no meaningful connection whatsoever to the resulting broader political culture of a given society
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Political socialization refers to the process through which individuals acquire political values and attitudes, while political culture refers to the resulting broader shared pattern of such values and attitudes across a given society, meaning the two concepts describe a process and its resulting outcome respectively

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the concept of “the state” is generally considered central to the broader academic discipline of Government, more so than the related concepts of “society” or “nation” alone?
options: The state, as a formally structured political and legal entity possessing sovereignty, government, defined territory, and population, is generally the primary institutional unit through which political power is organized and exercised, making it a particularly central focus for the study of Government as a discipline
The state generally holds no particular centrality whatsoever within the broader academic discipline of Government, compared to the concepts of society or nation
Society and nation are, in every respect, considerably more central to the discipline of Government than the concept of the state
The state, society, and nation are, in every respect, entirely interchangeable concepts holding an identical degree of centrality within the discipline
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: The state, as a formally structured political and legal entity possessing sovereignty, government, defined territory, and population, is generally the primary institutional unit through which political power is organized and exercised, making it a particularly central focus for the study of Government as a discipline

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding the specific historical circumstances under which fascism and Nazism arose in interwar Europe is considered valuable background, even within a West African-focused Government syllabus?
options: Understanding the particular historical, economic, and social conditions that can contribute to the rise of extreme, authoritarian ideologies provides valuable comparative insight applicable to recognizing similar warning signs in other historical or contemporary contexts, including within West Africa’s own political history
The historical circumstances surrounding the rise of fascism and Nazism in interwar Europe have no meaningful relevance whatsoever to a West African-focused Government syllabus
Extreme authoritarian ideologies generally arise entirely randomly, with no meaningful connection to identifiable underlying historical, economic, or social conditions
Comparative historical insight regarding the rise of fascism generally provides no meaningful analytical value whatsoever for understanding West African political history
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Understanding the particular historical, economic, and social conditions that can contribute to the rise of extreme, authoritarian ideologies provides valuable comparative insight applicable to recognizing similar warning signs in other historical or contemporary contexts, including within West Africa’s own political history

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why democracy is generally considered to require more than simply the existence of periodic elections alone?
options: Genuine democracy is generally understood to require not only elections but also broader features such as protection of civil liberties, the rule of law, and meaningful political competition, meaning elections alone, without these accompanying features, may not constitute genuine democratic governance
The mere existence of periodic elections, considered entirely in isolation from any other feature, is always fully sufficient to establish genuine democratic governance
Civil liberties and the rule of law have no meaningful connection whatsoever to whether a given political system qualifies as genuinely democratic
Meaningful political competition is, in principle, entirely unnecessary for a system to be properly classified as democratic
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Genuine democracy is generally understood to require not only elections but also broader features such as protection of civil liberties, the rule of law, and meaningful political competition, meaning elections alone, without these accompanying features, may not constitute genuine democratic governance

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why the concept of nationalism, as examined within this syllabus, is generally treated as closely intertwined with, though analytically distinct from, the related concept of colonialism?
options: Nationalism in the West African context substantially arose as a direct political response to colonial rule, meaning the two concepts are historically and causally closely connected, even though nationalism (a movement for self-determination) and colonialism (a system of external domination) remain analytically distinct concepts describing differing phenomena
Nationalism and colonialism are, in every respect, entirely identical concepts describing the exact same underlying historical phenomenon
Nationalism in West Africa arose entirely independently of, and with no meaningful historical connection whatsoever to, colonialism
The historical relationship between nationalism and colonialism generally has no meaningful bearing on how these two concepts are properly analytically distinguished
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Nationalism in the West African context substantially arose as a direct political response to colonial rule, meaning the two concepts are historically and causally closely connected, even though nationalism (a movement for self-determination) and colonialism (a system of external domination) remain analytically distinct concepts describing differing phenomena

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding the full range of basic concepts examined within this topic (power, authority, legitimacy, sovereignty, democracy, political culture, political socialization, and the various ideologies) is considered more analytically valuable than studying any single concept in isolation?
options: These concepts are interconnected and mutually reinforcing analytical tools, meaning understanding their interrelationships, rather than studying any single concept in isolation, provides a more complete and sophisticated foundation for analysing political systems

Studying any single one of these basic concepts in complete isolation provides an equally complete and sophisticated analytical foundation, compared to understanding the full range of concepts together
These various basic concepts are, in every respect, entirely unrelated to one another, requiring no combined or integrated study whatsoever
Interconnection among these basic concepts has no meaningful bearing on how effectively a student can analyse political systems
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: These concepts are interconnected and mutually reinforcing analytical tools, meaning understanding their interrelationships, rather than studying any single concept in isolation, provides a more complete and sophisticated foundation for analysing political systems

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why some newly independent West African governments’ embrace of socialist-inspired economic ideology in the 1960s is often understood partly as a reaction against the capitalist economic structures established during the colonial period?
options: Colonial economic structures were often designed primarily to serve the colonizing power’s own economic interests, meaning newly independent governments sometimes viewed socialist-inspired alternatives as a means of asserting greater national economic control and addressing colonial-era economic inequality
Colonial-era capitalist economic structures generally had no meaningful connection whatsoever to newly independent governments’ subsequent ideological choices

Newly independent West African governments generally embraced socialist-inspired ideology entirely independently of, and with no meaningful reference whatsoever to, their own preceding colonial economic experience
National economic control and colonial-era economic inequality are, in every respect, entirely unrelated considerations within the study of post- independence economic ideology
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Colonial economic structures were often designed primarily to serve the colonizing power’s own economic interests, meaning newly independent governments sometimes viewed socialist-inspired alternatives as a means of asserting greater national economic control and addressing colonial-era economic inequality

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why a clear understanding of the distinction between “power” and “authority” is considered particularly relevant to evaluating whether a given West African government, at a specific historical moment, ruled with genuine popular legitimacy?
options: Applying this conceptual distinction allows for a more precise historical evaluation of whether a given government’s rule rested primarily on coercive power alone, or on a broader, more genuine popular acceptance of its right to govern
The distinction between power and authority has no meaningful bearing whatsoever on how a historian or political analyst might evaluate a given government’s genuine popular legitimacy
Every government, by definition, always rules with an entirely identical degree of genuine popular legitimacy, rendering this particular conceptual distinction analytically unnecessary
Popular legitimacy is, in principle, an entirely undefinable, unanalysable historical or political phenomenon
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: Applying this conceptual distinction allows for a more precise historical evaluation of whether a given government’s rule rested primarily on coercive power alone, or on a broader, more genuine popular acceptance of its right to govern

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly explains why understanding basic concepts such as those examined within this topic is considered essential preparatory groundwork for the subsequent topic examining basic principles of government, such as the rule of law and separation of powers?
options: The basic principles examined in the following topic (such as the rule of law and separation of powers) are generally built upon, and expressed through, the more foundational concepts examined within this topic (such as power, authority, and legitimacy), meaning a prior grasp of these foundational concepts provides genuinely useful preparation
Basic concepts and basic principles of government are, in every respect, entirely unrelated topics requiring no meaningful sequential or connected study
The subsequent topic examining basic principles of government can be fully and adequately understood with no prior grounding whatsoever in this topic’s basic concepts
Foundational concepts such as power, authority, and legitimacy generally have no meaningful connection whatsoever to principles such as the rule of law or separation of powers
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: The basic principles examined in the following topic (such as the rule of law and separation of powers) are generally built upon, and expressed through, the more foundational concepts examined within this topic (such as power, authority, and legitimacy), meaning a prior grasp of these foundational concepts provides genuinely useful preparation

Basic Concepts of Government.text: Which of the following correctly summarizes the overall importance of understanding the broad range of basic concepts examined within this topic, spanning power, authority, legitimacy, sovereignty, democracy, political culture, political socialization, and the major political and economic ideologies?
options: A solid grounding in these basic concepts provides the essential analytical vocabulary and conceptual foundation necessary for meaningfully engaging with the more specific principles, institutions, and comparative West African political developments examined throughout the remainder of this syllabus
Understanding these basic concepts has no meaningful practical or academic value within the broader study of Government
Only a single one of these basic concepts is genuinely worthy of serious study, to the exclusion of all the others examined within this topic
These basic concepts bear no meaningful relationship to the more specific institutions or comparative political developments examined later within this syllabus
Basic Concepts of Government.correct_answer: A solid grounding in these basic concepts provides the essential analytical vocabulary and conceptual foundation necessary for meaningfully engaging with the more specific principles, institutions, and comparative West African political developments examined throughout the remainder of this syllabus

Basic Principles of Government.text: The rule of law is a foundational principle generally requiring that
options: the law applies unequally, favouring those who hold political power
everyone, including government officials, is subject to and accountable under the law, which is applied fairly and consistently
laws need not be publicly known or predictable
the executive arm of government is entirely exempt from any legal accountability
Basic Principles of Government.correct_answer: everyone, including government officials, is subject to and accountable under the law, which is applied fairly and consistently

Basic Principles of Government.text: Fundamental human rights generally refer to
options: privileges granted at the discretion of the government, which may be freely withdrawn at any time
basic rights and freedoms (such as life, liberty, and freedom of expression) generally considered inherent to all individuals, often given specific constitutional or legal protection
rights applicable exclusively to citizens holding public office
a concept with no meaningful connection to constitutional law
Basic Principles of Government.correct_answer: basic rights and freedoms (such as life, liberty, and freedom of expression) generally considered inherent to all individuals, often given specific constitutional or legal protection

Basic Principles of Government.text: Separation of powers is a principle generally requiring that
options: all governing power be concentrated within a single arm of government
governing power be divided among distinct arms of government (the legislature, executive, and judiciary), each with its own defined functions
only the executive arm of government should possess any meaningful power
power should be exercised exclusively by unelected officials
Basic Principles of Government.correct_answer: governing power be divided among distinct arms of government (the legislature, executive, and judiciary), each with its own defined functions

Basic Principles of Government.text: Checks and balances refers to the principle whereby
options: each arm of government operates in complete isolation, with no ability to influence or restrain the other arms
each arm of government is granted certain powers enabling it to monitor, restrain, or check the actions of the other arms, helping prevent abuse of power
all governing power is concentrated exclusively in the judiciary
only the legislature possesses any meaningful power to check other arms
Basic Principles of Government.correct_answer: each arm of government is granted certain powers enabling it to monitor, restrain, or check the actions of the other arms, helping prevent abuse of power

Basic Principles of Government.text: Constitutionalism refers to the principle that
options: government should operate free from any constitutional constraint whatsoever
government authority should be exercised in accordance with, and limited by, a constitution
only unwritten constitutions can meaningfully constrain government power
